statement: Built crates/enforcer-memory/src/search/search_graph.rs as the library-level search_graph(spec) entry point over CodeGraph, per docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/refs/x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md §2. Implements all three baseline modes (BM25 query, regex name_pattern+qn_pattern, semantic_query) with the exact mode-interaction fidelity: BM25 short-circuits and ignores name_pattern/label/degree filters and semantic_query once it has usable tokens and succeeds; falls through to the regex path only when BM25 finds zero usable tokens. The full filter set (label, file_pattern glob-or-bare-literal, relationship validated against ^[A-Z_]+$, min/max_degree with -1 sentinel, exclude_entry_points, include_connected 1-hop) is implemented on the regex path only, matching baseline. results/semantic_results are always separate lists, never merged.
why: The baseline C tool's docstring claims all three modes combine freely and defaults are 200 everywhere; tracing the actual C handler (already done by a prior extraction pass) shows BM25 short-circuits and its true default limit is 100. Porting the docstring instead of the code would silently diverge from the real contract every downstream caller will actually hit.
howToApply: When porting a tool wire contract from a baseline system, always trust the handler code path over the tool's own advertised docstring/schema description -- the extraction doc (x06-baseline-tool-schemas.md) explicitly flags where these disagree; treat those flagged discrepancies as the ground truth to port.

statement: enforcer-memory's CodeGraph (crates/enforcer-memory/src/code_graph.rs) models calls at FILE granularity (CallEdge::from_file_id -> callee-as-written-text, not a resolved target node id), unlike the baseline's resolved-node-id CALLS edges. This meant search_graph's degree computation, entry-point detection, and include_connected's 1-hop BFS all needed a best-effort callee-name-to-symbol-node resolution (resolve_callee_to_node_id, matching by symbol name only) rather than a real graph traversal. Also, this crate has no separate Class/Interface/Enum/Route labels -- only Function/Type/Test/File/TextOnly -- so the baseline's 4-label +5.0 BM25 boost tier collapses onto NodeLabel::Type alone here.
why: A future lane extending code_graph.rs to resolve calls to real target node ids (not just written text) would let search_graph's degree/entry-point/connected-names logic become exact instead of best-effort -- worth flagging as a known limitation rather than silently accepting approximate degree counts.
howToApply: If asked to improve search_graph's degree accuracy or trace_path (a future baseline tool) fidelity, first check whether code_graph.rs's CallEdge has grown resolved target ids; if not, that resolution pass is the real prerequisite, not another patch inside search_graph.rs itself.

statement: During this lane's work, crates/enforcer-memory/Cargo.toml and crates/enforcer-memory/src/lib.rs both had unresolved git merge conflict markers (HEAD vs bbe14fc, an x06.8/x06-trace federation checkpoint) that broke ALL builds of enforcer-memory crate-wide, not just x06-search's files. The coordination claim tool correctly queued an editIntent when x06-trace already held the write lock on the same shared files, and the conflicts resolved themselves within ~10-45 seconds once x06-trace's own work landed -- no manual intervention was needed beyond waiting and polling `grep -c '<<<<<<<'`.
why: Multiple concurrent lanes editing the same shared Cargo.toml/lib.rs files during an active rebase is expected and self-resolving under this coordination protocol; a worker hitting a merge-conflict-broken shared file should poll/wait rather than force a claim or attempt its own conflict resolution when another lane already holds the lock.
howToApply: If cargo build fails with 'expected item, found ==' or similar merge-marker errors in a shared file (Cargo.toml, lib.rs) that isn't in your own claimed-files list, check coordination claim status for that path first; if another lane holds the writeLock, poll briefly rather than racing to fix it yourself.
